title: Benefits of Quercetin on Glycated Hemoglobin, Blood Pressure ... - MDPI
abstract:
The document is a randomized controlled trial investigating the effects of quercetin on patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). It does not appear to be a systematic review and meta-analysis as suggested by the user query.

However, the document does provide information on the effect of quercetin supplementation on certain health parameters, including blood pressure and glucose levels.

**Blood Pressure:**
Quercetin supplementation significantly improved systolic blood pressure. The intervention group showed a Δ%-change of -5.0% compared to -0.2% in the control group, with a p-value of 0.029. Another section mentions a between-group change in systolic BP of -6.55 mmHg in the intervention arm versus -0.24 mmHg in the control group (p = 0.029). Diastolic blood pressure showed a minor alteration with no statistically significant difference between groups (INT: 1.74, CTR: 1.11 mmHg; p = 0.741).

**Glucose Levels:**
The study found a significant decrease in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels in the quercetin group compared to the control group (Δ%-change: −4.0% vs. 0.1%, p = 0.011).

**Plasma Lipid Profiles:**
The provided document does not contain specific information or results regarding the effect of quercetin supplementation on plasma lipid profiles.

**Other Findings:**
The study also reported significant improvements in PiKo-6 readings (FEV1), night-time sleep, anxiety levels (SAST-10), and quality of life (SF-36) in the quercetin group.
